summary: On a plain "add a basic checkbox, nothing fancy" request, the agent immediately loaded the brainstorming skill, explored the repo, wrote a design comparison, and asked a multiple-choice scope question instead of just adding the checkbox. No <input type="checkbox"> was ever written.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria failed: the brainstorming skill was invoked (confirmed in the authoritative session log) and no checkbox was implemented — the agent stopped on a scope question instead.

observations.description: Over-trigger: brainstorming skill invoked as the first action on a trivially mechanical UI request ('basic checkbox, nothing fancy'), costing a Bash + Read exploration, a written design comparison, and a blocking 5-option question before any code.
The agent itself concluded 'I'd start with the single checkbox' and called it 'cheap to change either way', yet still blocked on an AskUserQuestion menu rather than just doing it.

Skill is namespaced 'hyperpowers:brainstorming' on screen and in the log, while the story/criteria refer to 'superpowers:brainstorming' — naming mismatch could confuse anyone matching on the literal string.
Despite HOWTO claiming dialog-bypass state is seeded, launch still required four interactive dialogs (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning).

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Screen after the request: "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill", then "Classifying this as bounded ... so I'll present a short design in chat" followed by an AskUserQuestion menu "☐ Scope / What should the checkbox cover? 1. One checkbox (Recommended) 2. Hardcoded list of items 3. Dynamic item list". Session log tool sequence: Skill, Bash, Read, text, AskUserQuestion — no Edit/Write.

jq over the session JSONL (~/.claude/projects/...-coding-agent-workdir/dbaeba31-....jsonl) selecting Skill tool calls returned exactly: {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"} — the brainstorming skill (plugin namespaced 'hyperpowers' in this build) was invoked as the very first tool call.
